Decision model | Version 2.0 | 3 September 2026 | AUD, ex GST | First three 12-month periods after commercial readiness | Internal planning only

1. Use the Base case for operating planning, the Conservative case for survival cash and the Upside case only for capacity preparation.

2. Do not treat the offshore hourly fee as the full delivered cost. Retain the execution uplift, Australian consultant oversight, contingency, non-labour inputs and offshore privacy/security controls.

3. The Base plan supports positive Year 1 operating contribution after a detailed Australian cost base, but it requires an indicative working-capital reserve before tax/GST obligations.

4. Pricing remains internal and provisional. Approve entity/GST status, insurance, systems, payment stages, contractor terms, offshore access controls and exception authority before quoting.

How to use

• Update blue cells only.
• Record actual hours and vendor costs after each project.
• Review price and scope when expected GM falls below target.
• Ring-fence GST and tax cash.
• Hire or add contractor capacity from signed backlog, not forecast volume.
• Treat all offshore access as subject to approved contracts, privacy, security and client scope.

Direct cost includes role hours, a 25% offshore execution uplift, offer-specific non-labour cost, 10% delivery contingency and 1% payment/collection cost. The High case uses $100 consultant and $35 developer rates and is the pricing stress test.

Interpretation: the offshore model improves implementation economics, but the savings are not simply the difference between $100 and $35. The model retains explicit allowance for onboarding, security, FX/payment friction, rework, stabilisation and Australian consultant oversight. At the proposed planning prices every offer clears its target margin in the High rate case; validate hours and vendor costs after each engagement.
